Signal Processing.summary: In this paper, we propose a feedback-efficient hybrid precoding framework for wideband millimeter-wave (mmWave) multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems. To reduce the hardware cost of radio-frequency (RF) chains and the feedback burden associated with frequency-selective digital precoding, frequency-flat analog precoders and combiners are first constructed from the dominant angle-of-arrival (AoA) and angle-of-departure (AoD) directions associated with the strongest propagation paths. For digital precoding, a shared quantized codebook is designed using the Lloyd algorithm, and a binary-search-based hierarchical interpolation method is developed to identify codeword switching locations between adjacent pilot subcarriers. By avoiding exhaustive codeword comparisons over all intermediate subcarriers, the proposed method reduces online search complexity and enables compact digital-precoder feedback. For the considered system configuration, the proposed method achieves a worst-case feedback reduction of approximately 98.34% relative to full-grid per-subcarrier feedback. Simulation results further demonstrate competitive spectral efficiency and bit error rate (BER) performance, low computational cost, and robustness under imperfect effective channel state information (CSI).
Signal Processing.comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Accepted for presentation at the 2026 IEEE GLOBECOM Workshops

Signal Processing.title: Fluid Antennas Enabled UAV Communication Systems: Fundamentals, Challenges, and Future Directions
Signal Processing.summary: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) require uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems to adapt to large-scale propagation changes and fast local channel fluctuations. Fluid antennas (FAs) provide an additional degree of freedom (DoF) by reconfiguring antenna positions within a compact aperture. This article investigates FA-enabled UAV communication systems from the perspectives of fundamentals, design challenges, and future research directions. We first introduce a dual-mobility perspective, in which UAV trajectory planning provides macro-mobility for large-scale air-to-ground geometry adaptation, and FA position reconfiguration provides micro-mobility for fine-grained local channel adaptation. We then identify key design challenges arising from the high computational complexity and information uncertainty in the joint optimization of UAV trajectory, FA positions, and beamforming under mobility, energy, hardware, and security constraints. To address these challenges, we present a hybrid offline-online optimization framework, where prior information such as environment maps, user mobility patterns, and statistical channel state information (CSI) supports long-term planning, while real-time information such as instantaneous CSI and UAV state enables fast online correction. A case study on FA-enabled UAV-assisted vehicular communications demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework. Finally, we discuss future directions of FA-enabled UAV communication in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), secure communication, mobile edge computing (MEC), and aerial relaying.

Signal Processing.title: Wait to Learn: Timing the Gradient Return in Over-the-Air Split Learning over an Aging Single-Antenna Channel
Signal Processing.summary: In over-the-air split learning over an aging single-antenna Rayleigh channel, the mean returned gradient equals the antenna-domain gradient scaled by the temporal correlation. Uncorrected training collapses in negative-correlation lobes. Near a correlation zero, no nonzero scalar calibration improves the ratio of mean power to innovation power for an individual transmission, and, on the tested grid, using sixteen times as many pilots recovers only 7 percent of the training gap. Returning at the first correlation extremum with phase correction, 1.3 ms later at 3.5 GHz and 15 m/s, achieves 90.2 percent accuracy, compared with 91.8 percent with CSI. In the tested line-of-sight setting, the near-zero gap becomes negligible.
Signal Processing.comment: revised: theory reframed as instantiation of classical results, added line-of-sight extension

Signal Processing.title: Wait or Rotate: Statistical Repair of the Backward Pass in Over-the-Air Split Learning Under Channel Aging
Signal Processing.summary: Over-the-air split learning returns the receiver's loss gradient through the reciprocal channel, so terminal motion between the forward and backward transmissions corrupts the backward pass. We repair the aged return at a fixed receive array using only second-order statistics. Two numbers taken from the forward-backward cross-covariance, the alignment reachable by the best common phase and by the best unitary correction, bound the main term of every repair. In the 3GPP tapped-delay-line channels TDL-A/B/C, where every antenna ages by the same scalar, the two numbers coincide, and at a correlation zero all tested fixed corrections stay between 58% and 62% accuracy, whereas a return delayed to the next correlation lobe reaches 98.4%. In 3GPP clustered-delay-line channels a statistical unitary correction stays within 0.02 in mean cross-entropy of ideal channel knowledge in all six tested profile and speed combinations, while common-phase correction falls to 69% for CDL-A at 3 km/h and the tested delay loses up to 10 points. In a two-cluster model spatial correction is decisive only where the common-phase alignment nearly vanishes (64% to 95%). With a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10, only the delayed return trains at a separable correlation zero (86% against at most 16%), and at 30 km/h in a clustered-delay-line channel the unitary correction reaches 80% where the common phase reaches 60%. Given geometry, displacement and angular statistics, a port permutation chosen by linear assignment reaches 99.5-99.7% accuracy for hexagonal and square arrays in oblique motion without pilots or digital feedback during training, where nearest-position matching drops to 89%.
Signal Processing.comment: v2: substantially revised and retitled (v1: "Coherent but Discordant: Rotate, Don't Invert, to Backpropagate Through an Aging Channel"). Adds 3GPP TDL/CDL, matched-normalization and CIFAR-10 split-learning experiments. The v1 claim that unitary correction outperforms inversion is withdrawn. 9 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables

Signal Processing.title: BFLA: Block-Filtered Long-Context Attention Mechanism
Signal Processing.summary: We propose Block-Filtered Long-Context Attention (BFLA), a training-free sparse prefill method that combines deterministic Lightning-style block indexing, query-tile sharing, and length-adaptive Ratio-$K$ selection with block-sparse execution. BFLA evaluates attention using the original Q/K/V, requires no retraining or per-model parameter retuning, and integrates with vLLM while preserving native decoding. For fixed Q/K/V, we bound local attention-output error in terms of the omitted attention mass, indexer-score distortion, retention budget, and query-tile sharing. Evaluations on Gemma4-E4B-IT, Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.8-27B, and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next across LongBench-v2, RULER, InfiniteBench, and Terminal Bench 2.1 show BFLA matches or even outperforms dense baselines. BFLA shows up to approximately $4\times$ time-to-first-token and $3.72\times$ end-to-end request speedups over the corresponding dense-prefill baselines. Comparisons with state-of-the-art FlashPrefill V2 and Qwen Sparse Attention also demonstrate that BFLA has better performance and efficiency trade-offs. These findings highlight the value of BFLA for the acceleration of long-context serving. Project website: https://github.com/Alicewithrabbit/BFLA.
Signal Processing.comment: 28 pages, 9 tables, 2 figures

Signal Processing.title: Physics-Informed Structure Anchoring With Capture-Aware Prototype Calibration for Cross-Environment RF Fingerprinting
Signal Processing.summary: Radio frequency fingerprint identification (RFFI) exploits transmitter-specific hardware imperfections as physicallayer identity cues for Internet of Things (IoT) devices, but deep models often degrade across acquisition environments. In multi-antenna reception, antenna topology and frequencyoffset dynamics structure receiver observations, while capturedependent variation distorts target embeddings and misaligns source-trained decision boundaries. This article proposes physicsinformed structure anchoring with capture-aware prototype calibration (PISA-CAPC) to address both representation and decision mismatches. The two stages separate source representation construction from target decision correction. During source training, PISA organizes antenna tokens through a topology-guided graph, conditions propagation on CFO-derived acquisition dynamics, and applies bounded contextual residual suppression to preserve identity evidence. At deployment, unlabeled capture-aware prototype calibration (U-CAPC) estimates capture-local prototypes and recalibrates target decision scores while keeping the representation and source classifier fixed. Thus, calibration uses neither target labels nor target-domain backbone updates. On a measured WiFi benchmark with four receive antennas and ten transmitters, PISA-CAPC achieves a mean target-domain Macro-F1 of 0.9257 under a balanced transductive setting. Component ablations support complementary roles for topology-guided anchoring, CFO-conditioned modulation, reliability-aware token aggregation, contextual suppression, and capture-aware calibration. These results indicate that physically motivated representation learning can be combined with labelfree decision calibration to improve cross-environment RFFI under the evaluated protocol without changing the deployed backbone.
Signal Processing.comment: data needs to change

Signal Processing.title: Efficient SCA Algorithms for Sparse Bayesian Learning
Signal Processing.summary: Type-II sparse Bayesian learning (SBL) for the multiple measurement vector model recovers a sparse signal power vector by minimizing the marginal negative log-likelihood via the expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm, referred to as M-SBL. We revisit the covariance learning (CL) problem and develop three parallel first-order algorithms within the successive convex approximation (SCA) framework. CL-SCA minimizes per-coordinate surrogates formed by partially linearizing the log-determinant term, while CL-FP uses a damped projected fixed-point iteration derived from stationarity conditions. Both methods have closed-form updates. We prove that the fixed points of both update maps are exactly the KKT points of the CL problem, that each update direction satisfies a quantitative descent inequality, that the damped iterates achieve sufficient decrease with an $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1/2})$ best-iterate stationarity rate, and we derive a backtracking rule that retains this rate without step-size tuning. If damping factors are bounded away from zero, the residual vanishes along the whole sequence and every limit point is a KKT point. Local analysis motivates CL-Hyb, which combines CL-SCA and CL-FP. Experiments on device activity detection in massive random access show that CL-Hyb-bt matches the best CL solvers' accuracy at a fraction of the runtime and is over an order of magnitude faster than EM.

Signal Processing.title: How Much Sensing is Enough? Landslide Detection from Sparse and Noisy 3D Observations
Signal Processing.summary: Dense 3D terrain information is critical for accurate landslide detection; however, acquiring such data at large scale is often limited by sensing infrastructure, coverage, and environmental conditions. Emerging sensing modalities (e.g., mmWave, low-cost radar, sparse LiDAR) can operate under adverse conditions, but inherently produce sparse and noisy 3D observations, raising an important question: \emph{how much sensing is sufficient for reliable landslide detection?} Given the absence of large-scale sparse-terrain datasets, we have constructed a physics-informed dataset by combining digital elevation models from OpenTopography with soil moisture data from NASA's SMAP. Subsequently, we have randomly generated landslide events and introduced controlled sparsification and stochastic noise to emulate sensing constraints. We have then developed a learning-based framework to reconstruct the underlying terrain and identify landslide-prone regions using a CNN + XGBoost method. Our results show that with only 20\% of the original observations, the proposed method achieves a detection accuracy of 80\% and a ROC-AUC of 0.868, with a reconstruction error (L2 Chamfer Distance) of 99.67~$m^2$ on the test set. We have further studied the impact of sparsity, highlighting the trade-off between sensing density and detection performance.

Signal Processing.title: AgriDefend: A $205 Offline Edge Device that Detects Crop Stress Before Visible Symptoms via Multimodal AI Fusion
Signal Processing.summary: Most in-field crop-monitoring devices sense a single modality -- either a camera looking at the canopy or a probe reading the soil -- and so cannot detect stress that begins below ground before it becomes visible above it. We present AgriDefend, a self-contained consumer-grade edge device that fuses both. A MobileNetV2 convolutional neural network (CNN) analyses canopy imagery, and a Random Forest classifier integrates trend features from a single soil probe: moisture, the rate of change in pH and in N, P, K, and belowground CO2 relative to ambient (a proxy for soil respiration). A logistic-regression meta-learner fuses the two into a five-class crop-health prediction, all on a Raspberry Pi 5 with no cloud or cellular link. On a controlled greenhouse drought trial with wild radish, the fused model reached 87% accuracy (R^2=0.88, MAE=0.05) at 1.4 s INT8 TensorFlow Lite inference, and its soil signals preceded visible wilting by about four days. The complete bill of materials is $205, roughly a fifth of comparable commercial nodes, positioning multimodal, sustainable crop sensing as a practical consumer-electronics product for connectivity-limited settings.
Signal Processing.comment: 3 pages, 3 figures

Signal Processing.title: Energy-Efficient Risk-Constrained Adaptive Semantic Communications Under Uncertain Adversarial Threats
Signal Processing.summary: Semantic communication systems based on deep joint source-channel coding can provide task-oriented wireless transmission, but adversarial robustness may require substantial radio and receiver-side defensive-computation energy. This paper develops an energy-efficient, risk-constrained semantic communication framework under source-domain, over-the-air (OTA), and potentially composite adversarial conditions. Long-term total energy, including communication and diffusion-purification energy, is minimized subject to average semantic-loss, trajectory-level tail-risk, and end-to-end latency constraints. A recurrent primal-dual proximal policy optimization controller jointly adapts transmit power, semantic/channel bandwidth ratio, and purification complexity using causal channel observations, semantic confidence, imperfect attack-belief estimates, and recurrent history. A conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) constraint explicitly limits severe semantic failures. On CIFAR-100, at the unseen source-domain level $ε=12/255$, the proposed controller achieves approximately $61\%$ robust Top-1 accuracy with $\mathrm{CVaR}_{0.9}\approx0.36$ while using about $9\%$ less total energy than diffusion-only defense. At the unseen OTA level $Γ_A=-5$ dB, it achieves approximately $52\%$ robust Top-1 accuracy, reduces semantic tail risk by $40\%$, and consumes about $8\%$ less total energy than diffusion-only defense. These results demonstrate energy-efficient semantic defense under partially observable adversarial conditions.

Signal Processing.title: Physical Adjoint Learning in Wave Systems with Asymmetric Couplings
Signal Processing.summary: Developing self-optimizing physical systems that learn directly from their response to external stimuli offers a promising route toward adaptive and intelligent machines. A key ingredient is the ability to evaluate optimization gradients within the physical hardware, bypassing the need for accurate numerical models. In wave systems, \textit{in-situ} adjoint methods provide this capability by exploiting reciprocity to physically realize the adjoint dynamics. However, this approach generally breaks down in nonreciprocal systems, where the adjoint field cannot be directly accessed through the original device. Here, we develop an \textit{in-situ} adjoint optimization framework that extends physical gradient computation to wave systems with asymmetric couplings through computationally low-cost similarity transformations between the forward and transposed operators. We utilize available degrees of freedom like tailored injected excitations, targeted measurements, and tunable parameters, to enable adjoint field reconstruction through forward experiments on the same physical platform. We demonstrate the versatility of the protocol through broadband transmission and isolation, coherent perfect absorption, programmable wavefront shaping, and spatially selective sensing. Our results provide a route to self-optimization in complex nonreciprocal wave systems through efficient physical gradient-based learning. The number of experiments required by the protocol does not increase with the number of optimization parameters, and the method remains applicable even when parts of the system are completely inaccessible.
Signal Processing.comment: Main text: 13 pages, 7 figures; (+) Supplementary Information: 5 pages, 1 figure

Signal Processing.title: C-MambaPose: Phase-Preserving Complex Mamba for Cross-Environment Wi-Fi Human Pose Estimation
Signal Processing.summary: Cross-environment generalization remains a fundamental challenge for Wi-Fi-based human pose estimation (HPE), as environmental multipath can drastically alter Channel State Information (CSI) for the same human motion. Existing approaches often discard CSI phase or collapse complex signals into real-valued features early, losing motion-sensitive phase dynamics. We present C-MambaPose, a phase-preserving complex-valued state-space framework for robust cross-environment Wi-Fi 3D HPE. Our key insight is to preserve complex phase relationships throughout spatiotemporal modeling, rather than using phase only as an input feature. C-MambaPose sanitizes synchronization-induced phase errors and employs a Spatiotemporal Complex Mamba encoder with dynamic multi-scale receptive fields to capture long-range phase-amplitude dynamics. Cross-attention then maps the learned representations to human joints, followed by a skeleton-aware GraFormer decoder for anatomically coherent pose estimation. Experiments on MM-Fi show that C-MambaPose achieves strong performance across all settings, with the largest gains in unseen environments, reaching $298.5$ mm and $317.6$ mm MPJPE on the two cross-environment protocols using only $3.78$ M parameters and no pretraining. Ablations further show that prematurely discarding complex phase relationships substantially degrades performance, demonstrating their importance for cross-environment Wi-Fi HPE.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted to IEEE RIVF 2026

Signal Processing.title: Radio Resource Allocation for Beam Hopping Scheduling in LEO Satellite Communications: A Spatio-Temporal Perspective
Signal Processing.summary: Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks face critical challenges in radio resource allocation due to dynamic traffic demands and stringent interference constraints. Beam-hopping (BH) technology offers a promising solution by enabling dynamic beam resource allocation across spatial and temporal domains. In this paper, we propose a Tabu Search-based spatio-temporal BH resource allocation strategy for LEO satellite communication systems. Specifically, the BH scheduling problem is formulated to maximize user demand satisfaction under interference constraints. To solve this problem efficiently, the proposed Tabu Search framework integrates adaptive tabu tenure control, greedy-based initialization with interference-aware beam selection, and Simulated Annealing acceptance criteria. Extensive simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves system throughput by 17.2\% and user satisfaction by 11.7\% compared with greedy-based BH strategies. These results indicate that the proposed approach provides a scalable and robust solution for dynamic resource allocation in interference-limited LEO satellite networks.

Signal Processing.title: A Unified Channel Model and Performance Evaluation for Underwater-to-Air Optical Links
Signal Processing.summary: This paper develops a conditional statistical framework for nominally normal underwater-to-air optical links. It combines bulk attenuation, normalized log-normal atmospheric and Weibull underwater fluctuations, and entrance-pupil collection with surface-tilt-dependent Fresnel transmission. Conditioning transmission and beam displacement on a common tilt preserves their dependence. Product distributions with explicit support and Jacobians yield integrals valid for arbitrary positive Weibull shape. Average uncoded OOK bit error rate (BER) and outage are evaluated using consistent power, noise and SNR definitions. Independent component-wise Monte Carlo verifies the full conditional model at six reference configurations; targeted importance sampling checks selected BER values down to approximately 6 x 10^-9. A circular-pupil Gaussian integral reveals parameter-dependent errors in the equivalent-beam collection approximation, including a 36.9% BER underestimate at one tested operating point. Conditional power and distance studies therefore use the circular-pupil reference and distinguish low-error short-air-segment conditions from collection-limited conditions. Source-anchored spectral and water-type contrasts, together with illumination and receiver checks, identify the dependence of these results on the prescribed operating conditions. The framework supplies reproducible error and outage calculations within a single-patch scalar model; physical operating ranges additionally depend on the surface, propagation and receiver assumptions.

Signal Processing.title: Movable-Element Multi-Functional RIS-Assisted Hybrid RSMA-NOMA: A Constrained Hybrid Reinforcement Learning Approach
Signal Processing.summary: In this work, we propose a movable-element (ME) multi-functional reconfigurable intelligent surface (MF-RIS) architecture, termed MM-RIS, which integrates element mobility with adaptive signal reflection, transmission, amplification, and energy harvesting (EH) to enhance communication flexibility and energy self-sustainability. A hybrid rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) transmission scheme is further designed to improve spectral efficiency. We formulate an energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem by jointly optimizing transmit beamforming, power and rate allocation, MM-RIS configurations, panel deployment, and ME positions. To address the resulting non-convex mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem, we propose constrained hybrid deep reinforcement learning with federated transformer and parametrized sharing (CRAFTS). CRAFTS integrates multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) and multi-agent deep Q-networks (MADQN) through bi-directional parametrized sharing to handle continuous and discrete actions, respectively. Moreover, a transformer-based architecture and federated learning (FL) are incorporated to enhance state representation and distributed knowledge sharing, whilst a Lagrangian-based adaptive penalty mechanism facilitates the constraint satisfaction. Simulation results have demonstrated that the proposed MM-RIS architecture and CRAFTS framework substantially improve EE and constraint satisfaction compared to the benchmarks in the open literature. Moreover, the results validate the benefits of spatially reconfigurable MM-RIS, hybrid RSMA-NOMA transmissions, and intelligent collaborative learning, highlighting the potential of the proposed framework for energy-efficient and adaptive next-generation wireless networks.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted by IEEE TCOM

Systems and Control.title: Programmable Sequential Memory in Coupled Oscillator Networks
Systems and Control.summary: The Hopfield network established that static memories can be stored as energy minima of an energy-based model. Real intelligent agents, however, must navigate sequences of memories rather than isolatedcsnapshots. Biological cortex addresses this through a separation of timescales, where fast synaptic dynamics encode individual states while slow neuromodulatory processes govern transitions between them. Inspired by this organization, we propose a sequential memory architecture that is fully continuous and admits exponential storage capacity. The architecture is programmable, since the transition structure is carried by a mechanism that is decoupled from the stored patterns, driven by the input context, and free to be chosen, optimized, or learned from data. Specifically, we construct an autonomous three-timescale dynamical system with three coupled layers. A fast Kuramoto layer stores phase patterns as exponentially stable phase-locked configurations, an intermediate recognition layer sets the dwell times, and a slow attention layer routes the transitions. We analyze the stability, dwell time, and capacity of the system, and we validate the dynamics through numerical simulations of sequential memory retrieval.

Systems and Control.title: A 2-DOF MultiBody Track Joint for Race Car Optimization
Systems and Control.summary: TrackJoint is a Modelica MultiBody component that turns a three-dimensional road surface into a joint with two degrees of freedom. The two joint coordinates are the distance travelled along a reference line and the sideways offset from that line. Together they give the position, orientation and angular velocity of a single frame_b connector. All road geometry reaches the joint as a small set of periodic piecewise-quintic splines, so one component can represent any circuit whose splines have been fitted beforehand. The road constraint is closed with d'Alembert's principle. The two generalized forces that belong to the joint coordinates are set to zero, so no Lagrange multipliers are needed. The joint is connected to a multibody race car in Dymola and the pair is exported as one FMI~3.0 FMU. The same FMU is then used for time-domain simulation and for CasADi/IPOPT minimum lap-time optimization, with no change to the model in between. This works because the joint keeps the arc-length coordinate as a real state and publishes its time derivative, which is the quantity that lets the problem be rewritten with distance We report results for minimum lap time simulations on the Singapore Formula~1 circuit.

Systems and Control.title: Gradient-Free Neural Hamilton-Jacobi Reachability for Scalable Safety-Critical Control
Systems and Control.summary: Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability provides a principled framework for synthesizing safety certificates and robust controllers for safety-critical robotic systems. However, applying reachability analysis to high-dimensional nonlinear systems remains challenging: classical grid-based solvers suffer from the curse of dimensionality, continuous-time neural solvers require accurate spatial value gradients, and reinforcement-learning-based approaches often suffer from weak boundary anchoring and non-stationary adversarial policy optimization. We propose a discrete-time neural reachability framework for control-disturbance-affine systems that learns backward reachable tubes (BRTs) and backward reach-avoid tubes (BRATs) through Bellman-Isaacs value propagation. Our key idea is to combine equation-driven self-supervision with structured policy learning: rather than computing explicit PDE-gradients, we exploit the bang-bang structure of optimal safety interventions to construct approximate teacher actions from gradient-free value probes, converting adversarial actor learning into supervised policy learning. To stabilize long-horizon value propagation, we leverage the learned actor to train the value function backward from the terminal boundary using a windowed temporal curriculum, where each window is used as the boundary condition for the next window. Across benchmark problems up to 80 dimensions, our method learns accurate reachability value functions while improving stability over existing learning-based solvers. We further demonstrate observation-space scalability on F1-tenth racing with over 16,000-dimensional egocentric inputs. The learned safety filter generalizes zero-shot to unseen tracks and transfers to a physical RC car, achieving real-time robust collision avoidance.

Systems and Control.title: Data-Driven Hamiltonian for Neural Optimal Control
Systems and Control.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as a prominent data-driven approach to optimal control, but often requires substantial amounts of data and provides limited guarantees when encountering out-of-distribution state-action pairs. In this paper, we propose an alternative approach grounded in the well-established Hamilton-Jacobi framework in optimal control theory. Rather than requiring an explicit analytical model of the system dynamics to evaluate the Hamiltonian, we replace this with a data-driven Hamiltonian (DDH), which we generalize to a broad class of optimal control problems. In contrast to standard RL approaches, the DDH provides a principled mechanism, requiring only minimal prior system information such as a Lipschitz constant, for quantifying and accounting for uncertainty in regions not covered by the data, enabling the derivation of controllers with performance guarantees. Additional prior system knowledge, when available, can be readily incorporated to improve performance. For high-dimensional systems, we further introduce a physics-informed neural approximation of the value function, trained using a novel procedure that generates worst-case fictitious rollouts evaluated through the DDH. On an LQR problem, the DDH reaches near-optimal cost on every dataset we test, including random data on which offline RL methods remain far from optimal, and needs far fewer samples than online RL. On a nonlinear lunar lander benchmark, the DDH achieves an optimality gap to a trajectory-optimization reference more than $3\times$ smaller than CQL and FQL, and matches the performance of SAC with approximately $37\times$ fewer samples. These results establish the DDH as a promising framework for data-driven optimal control, particularly in settings where available data are limited in quantity or quality.

Systems and Control.title: Multi-time-scale Control of Power Systems
Systems and Control.summary: The power grid has been dominated by large synchronous generators and clearly separated control layers. Today, power-electronics energy conversion interfaces are rapidly being deployed calling for another look at system-level control hierarchies. This article examines how multi-time-scale modeling, feedback control, and feedback optimization can help reinterpret the traditional organically grown hierarchy of primary control, automatic generation control, and economic dispatch, and enable new approaches for control of contemporary power systems. Beginning with an overview of power system models and conventional operational practices, the article develops connections to modern control architectures that can coordinate heterogeneous resources, account for operational constraints, and exploit faster actuation without overlooking first-principles physics.

Systems and Control.title: Distribution Grid Reconfiguration and Restoration via Linearizable Multi-phase Power Flow Modeling
Systems and Control.summary: Accurate and tractable power-flow (PF) modeling is essential for distribution grid topology optimization, where the presence of discrete branch-status decisions therein significantly increase the computational complexity. To tackle this challenge, we develop a topology-adaptive, low-complexity neural piecewise-linear (N-PWL) PF model. We propose a sequential layer design that can directly incorporate branch status variables into the PF mapping from branch flows to nodal injections. As a result, our N-PWL model not only preserves the PF branch-node consistency but also facilitates the representation of any unseen topologies without retraining. A low-complexity model design is further pursued to attain a linear NN parameter scaling by using a fixed-size area partition of the feeder. The resulting scalable N-PWL model enables mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations of feeder topology optimization tasks, including distribution network reconfiguration (DNR) and restoration ordering problems (ROP). Numerical studies on the unbalanced, multi-phase IEEE 123-bus feeder demonstrate our N-PWL model outperforms existing end-to-end baselines in PF prediction and, more importantly, can fill the gap by achieving accurate representation of any unseen topologies. For solving DNR/ROP, our model can significantly improve the AC feasibility over linearized PF models, with a notable reduction of computation time compared with AC-PF based nonlinear formulations, particularly under a large number of topology decisions.

Systems and Control.title: Improving Learned AC-OPF Feasibility under Distribution Shift with PF-in-the-Loop Correction
Systems and Control.summary: Learning-based AC-OPF enables fast dispatch, yet its feasibility can degrade under distribution shift. We analyze three state-of-the-art methods and identify a shared deployment-time limitation: none use feedback from the power-flow (PF)-realized state to ensure feasibility of the predicted control. Using a simple PF-in-the-loop feasibility restoration filter, we empirically show that such feedback substantially improves hard feasibility across four out-of-distribution scenarios with modest runtime overhead.

Systems and Control.title: A Benchmark Library for Distributed Power System Analysis and Optimization
Systems and Control.summary: DPLib is an open-source benchmark library created to support research and development in distributed power system analysis and optimization. Unlike centralized tools such as MATPOWER and PGLib, no general purpose, reproducible data library package currently exists for distributed power system studies. DPLib, available at \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/DPLib.git}{GitHub}, fills this gap by providing 40 multi-region benchmark test cases ranging from 5 buses to 20758 buses, along with a graph-based partitioning toolkit that converts MATPOWER-compatible systems into distributed regional datasets. The toolkit generates standardized \texttt{.mat}, \texttt{.csv}, and \texttt{.m} files, regional MATPOWER version 2 cases, local and global bus mappings, generator and cost assignments, explicit inter-regional tie-line records, and bus-to-region partition maps. It supports unweighted, electrically weighted, and user-defined partitions, and is compared with METIS, KaFFPa, and an IPA-inspired baseline. DPLib also provides ADMM-based distributed DC and AC OPF solvers for validation. Numerical studies report partitioning sensitivity, centralized run times, distributed OPF iterations, run times, and optimality gaps. These results establish DPLib as a reproducible data layer for distributed power system research.

Systems and Control.title: Ctrl-A: Control-Driven Machine Learning using Adaptive Online Data Augmentation
Systems and Control.summary: We introduce ControlAugment (Ctrl-A), an automated data augmentation algorithm for image-vision tasks, which incorporates principles from control theory for online adjustment of augmentation strength distributions during model training. Ctrl-A eliminates the need for initialization of individual augmentation strengths. Instead, augmentation strength distributions are dynamically, and individually, adapted during training based on a control-loop architecture and what we define as relative operation response curves. Using an operation-dependent update procedure provides Ctrl-A with the potential to reduce the use of augmentation operations that negatively impact model performance, alleviating the need to manually engineer augmentation policies for new image classification tasks. Experiments on the CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN-core, and Tiny ImageNet benchmark datasets using WideResNet-28-10 and ResNet architectures demonstrate that Ctrl-A provides competitive performance across a range of image classification benchmarks.
Systems and Control.comment: 19 pages (13 pages main manuscript), 12 figures (9 in main manuscript). v2 note: Title slightly changed to make it less generic/more descriptive. Experimental section overhauled to demonstrate and exemplify closed-loop control mechanism, experiment with Tiny ImageNet added

Systems and Control.title: Reach-Avoid Differential game with Reachability Analysis for UAVs: A decomposition approach
Systems and Control.summary: Reach-avoid (RA) games have significant applications in security and defense, particularly for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). These problems are inherently challenging due to the need to consider obstacles, consider the adversarial nature of opponents, ensure optimality, and account for nonlinear dynamics. Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) reachability analysis has emerged as a powerful tool for tackling these challenges; however, while it has been applied to games involving two spatial dimensions, directly extending this approach to three spatial dimensions is impossible due to high dimensionality. On the other hand, alternative approaches for solving RA games lack the generality to consider games with three spatial dimensions involving agents with non-trivial system dynamics. In this work, we propose a novel framework for dimensionality reduction by decomposing the problem into a horizontal RA sub-game and a vertical RA sub-game. We then solve each sub-game using HJ reachability analysis and consider second-order dynamics that account for the defender's acceleration. To reconstruct the solution to the original RA game from the sub-games, we introduce a HJ-based tracking control algorithm in each sub-game that not only guarantees capture of the attacker but also tracking of the attacker thereafter. We prove the conditions under which the capture guarantees are maintained. The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated via numerical simulations, showing that the decomposition maintains optimality and guarantees in the original problem. Our methods are also validated in a Gazebo physics simulator, achieving successful capture of quadrotors in three spatial dimensions space for the first time to the best of our knowledge.
Systems and Control.comment: Paper version 1 accepted to the Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics (JGCD). Version 2 strengthens the horizontal invariance and updates figures in the experiment

Systems and Control.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
Systems and Control.summary: Many everyday tasks require controlling contact force as well as motion. On a humanoid, this force must often be coordinated across both hands and the whole body, and cannot be specified by kinematic trajectories alone. Therefore, we present FLORE, a framework for learning force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation. We collect robot-free demonstrations using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers for hand motion and contact wrenches, and wearable trackers for body motion. A force-reactive diffusion policy takes vision, proprioception, and measured wrenches as input, then predicts actions and per-hand force commands. A hybrid compliance whole-body controller with force tracking executes these commands while maintaining balance: an integral of the force error measured by real force/torque (F/T) sensors lets each hand track force accurately along the commanded direction and remain compliant along the others. In simulation, the controller tracks per-hand force commands of varied magnitude and direction, with little loss in whole-body motion accuracy. Across three contact-rich tasks on the robot, the force-reactive policy succeeds in 80% of rollouts, compared with 26.7% for a position-only policy trained on the same demonstrations and executed by the same controller. For more details, please visit our website: https://louis-leee.github.io/FLoRe/.

Systems and Control.title: Nonprehensile Robotic Catching Using Virtual Constraints
Systems and Control.summary: The problem of nonprehensile robotic catching is addressed using virtual nonholonomic constraints (VNHCs); the motion of the robot end-effector is designed and controlled directly in terms of the states of the object before it is caught on the surface of the end-effector. In contrast to contemporary approaches, our approach avoids the need for object trajectory prediction, and consequent time-varying robot trajectory generation. With a focus on the planar case, we demonstrate that our VNHC approach can be used to catch an object on an end-effector at a desired height, with minimal relative normal velocity at the contact instant. Moreover, the VNHC function depends only on the desired catching height, and the same VNHC can be used for a range of initial conditions. We use model predictive control (MPC) to bring the object and end-effector to rest at a desired location after contact is made. The approach is validated in simulation.
Systems and Control.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures; an abridged version of this article has been submitted to the 2027 American Control Conference (ACC)

Systems and Control.title: Formalizing and Estimating Task-Space Complexity for Zero-shot Generalization
Systems and Control.summary: Generalization is crucial for modern control, but learning across tasks can be costly. Recent work shows that zero-shot transfer, in which a controller designed for a source task is directly deployed to a target task, can achieve strong performance. We formalize task-space complexity, which characterizes the difficulty of achieving sufficiently good performance across a collection of tasks, by casting source selection as a covering problem. We provide bounds on the complexity and demonstrate its applicability.

Systems and Control.title: Security Region Compression via Hybrid Vertex Pruning for Enhanced Computational Efficiency
Systems and Control.summary: The security region (SR) specifies a joint feasible region in the operational space involving various installations within the power system. It enables dynamic allocation of capacity among these energy units, thereby unlocking additional grid potential for power delivery and mitigating congestion. By constructing a convex hull from a set of vertices to form a polytope, the SR can be effectively represented with an acceptable accuracy loss. However, the SR computation inevitably generates many low-quality vertices, which contribute little to the overall hypervolume and can be discarded. By introducing SR compression, the SR data size can be reduced, which in turn facilitates the memory-efficient computation of SR and time-efficient solution of SR-related optimization problems. Accordingly, this paper proposes a vertex pruning approach that mixes local and backward search policies to achieve effective SR compression. In particular, the backward search strategy allows previously pruned vertices to be recycled when they are re-identified as critical. Subsequently, we incorporate this approach to enhance computational efficiency in the aforementioned applications. Numerical validations are conducted on two realistic medium-voltage Dutch grid cases. The results demonstrate at most 1.65% hypervolume loss with over 96.0\% SR data size reduction after applying the proposed compression approach. Empowered by this compression, the 8-dimensional (8D) SR becomes computationally tractable. Moreover, in relevant grid-aware computation challenges, the solving time can be reduced by at least 52.9% with at most an 1.36% optimality loss. All above validate both the efficacy and values of the proposed SR compression approach.

Systems and Control.title: World Model for Energy Efficiency Maximization in Dynamic Metasurface Antennas
Systems and Control.summary: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) have emerged as a promising technology for realizing large-scale antenna arrays in next-generation wireless networks owing to their ability to enable dense and energy-efficient antenna architectures. However, jointly optimizing digital beamforming and DMA element weights under time-varying channel conditions remains challenging due to their coupled effects on the received signal and interference powers. We formulate this problem to maximize time-averaged energy efficiency (EE) under time-varying channel conditions, subject to transmit power constraints, Lorentzian phase limitations, and minimum rate requirements. To enable long-term planning and improve sample efficiency compared with model-free reinforcement learning, we develop a world model framework that learns latent system dynamics from interactions with the environment and jointly optimizes digital beamforming and DMA element weights through imagined trajectories. Furthermore, we incorporate feasibility-preserving action mappings and safety cost signals to ensure constraint satisfaction during policy learning. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves the time-averaged EE by approximately 20% compared with the deep Q-network baseline, while achieving higher sample efficiency and more reliable constraint satisfaction.

Systems and Control.title: Repeated Binary Direct Collinear Impacts Under Incremental Contact Laws With Residual Indentation: A Hybrid Systems Formulation
Systems and Control.summary: Incremental contact laws specify the normal contact force through a differential relation, possibly carrying an internal state, driven by the indentation and its rate. In some, the force is extinguished at a nonzero indentation, whether by plastic deformation or by an elastic aftereffect, so that a residual deformation remains at separation. Such laws sit uneasily within rigid body dynamics, which admits no deformation. The tension is tolerable when the indentation is small relative to the bodies, so that it may be carried constitutively rather than geometrically. Even then, the contact law alone does not determine the interaction of the bodies. Because force and indentation no longer vanish together, conditions for the commencement and termination of contact must be supplied separately. So must the fate of the deformation and internal state at separation, neither of which the equations of motion contain. This article formulates the repeated direct collinear impact of two convex bodies under external forces as a hybrid dynamical system. The contact interface is modeled as a massless element carrying the contact law and its state, coupled to the bodies through relative velocity and an interaction force dictated by the contact state. Consequently, all switching and resets are confined to the interface, leaving the geometry and the equations of motion of the bodies unaltered. The principal analytical properties of the resulting formulations are established, among them passivity and completeness; the branching of solutions at the onset and termination of contact is also examined. The framework is demonstrated through numerical simulations.
Systems and Control.comment: 30 pages, 6 figures; v1-v5: a variety of amendments and corrections; v6: additional analytical properties of the contact laws used in examples

Systems and Control.title: A Novel Path-Tracking Algorithm for Automated Tractor-Trailer Forward and Backward Maneuvers
Systems and Control.summary: Fully autonomous tractor-trailer systems are increasingly deployed in logistics, agriculture, and industrial environments, where precise and robust path-tracking capabilities are essential. However, the articulation between the tractor and the trailer introduces additional nonlinearities and significantly complicates lateral and longitudinal control, particularly during reversing maneuvers. This paper introduces a novel path-tracking algorithm specifically designed for articulated vehicles with a single trailer. The proposed method combines a lateral control law applied at the trailer level with a short-horizon predictive adjustment of the tractor steering angle, ensuring stable convergence toward the desired path in both forward and backward motion. The approach is geometry-based and requires no per-vehicle calibration or training. Simulation studies in a high-fidelity physics simulator show steady-state or final lateral errors of $0.02$--$0.05$~m on straight-line, circular, and reverse docking trajectories, which is of the same order of magnitude as, or lower than, the errors reported in the literature. Real-world experiments on a small-scale tractor--trailer robot, with the whole controller running on a low-cost microcontroller, further confirm the feasibility of the approach, with lateral errors below 13~mm during repeated reverse docking maneuvers despite a pose detection latency of about 200~ms.

Systems and Control.title: Grid-Forming AC/DC Converters for Meshed DC Networks via Dual-Measurement Frequency Droop
Systems and Control.summary: This paper proposes and analyzes a dual-measurement frequency-droop (DMFD) controller for meshed MVDC networks. Using only two local DC measurements, bus-voltage deviation and a filtered DC-port current or power deviation, the controller enables grid-forming operation at both AC and DC ports across the mesh. Although the DMFD regulates neither the DC voltage nor the DC current directly and acts only on the terminal frequency, it is shown that AC-side synchronization closes an effective DC droop at every synchronized terminal, so that the steady operating point of the mesh exists and is unique. Constant frequency deviations at a terminal and single-terminal islanding enter the same DC equations as equivalent current offsets, with the island frequency fixed by the island power balance, allowing node voltages and branch currents to be obtained from one linear system. The steady-state model yields design-use envelopes to map the droop ratios and the net DC-injection levels into bounds on DC-voltage deviation and terminal currents. A small-signal dynamic model is developed and used to generate eigenvalue loci and damping-ratio charts that guide controller-gain selection. Averaged EMT simulations on a four-terminal ring corroborate the analysis: in regimes where PLL-based grid-following control is known to lose damping, the DMFD controller maintains stable operation and follows the predicted steady-state characteristics.

Systems and Control.title: FedAvgIm: Federated Learning for Multi-Site Impedance Identification of Inverter-Based Resources
Systems and Control.summary: With the increasing integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) into power systems, assessing small-signal interaction stability has become essential. Impedance/admittance models enable frequency-domain characterization of IBR dynamics without requiring access to proprietary internal control details, but measurement-based identification is time-consuming and must be repeated across operating points. This paper proposes FedAvgIm, a privacy-aware federated-learning framework for multi-site dq-admittance identification under severe local data scarcity and raw-data-locality constraints. Each IBR site trains a local feed-forward neural network using a small set of operating-point-frequency samples, while only model parameters are shared with a cloud aggregator that performs sample-size-weighted FedAvg to update a global model and broadcast it back to all sites. To demonstrate effectiveness, EMT measurement-based admittance datasets are constructed for nine grid-following IBRs with different parameters, architectures, measurement-noise levels, and non-IID settings, where each client has only 40-390 training samples. Results show that FedAvgIm achieves performance close to centralized training and consistently outperforms local-only learning and raw-data-locality-preserving transfer-learning baselines. Additional studies show that FedAvgIm maintains stable learning behavior under measurement noise and remains beneficial under moderate non-IID conditions. The estimated dq-admittance models are further applied to generalized Nyquist stability analysis and validated against EMT time-domain simulations under multiple operating points and grid-strength conditions.
Systems and Control.comment: Author-accepted manuscript (not the IEEE version of record)

Systems and Control.title: Efficient ADMM for Soft-Constrained Quadratic Programs via Generalized Slack Projections
Systems and Control.summary: Quadratic programs (QPs) are a core building block in many applications. In practice, constraints are often softened with slack variables to guarantee feasibility. The standard approach tackles this by introducing additional decision variables, growing the resulting optimization problem. In this paper, we propose an Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) scheme for a broad class of convex slack penalty functions, including all $\ell_k$-norms, without increasing the problem size. The only change to the ADMM scheme is a modified slack projection function, while the remaining algorithm stays the same. We demonstrate our approach on numerical examples, showing significant speedups, and show its flexibility on an energy optimization problem.

Systems and Control.title: Rethinking electrified transportation: The case for dynamic wireless charging
Systems and Control.summary: Long-term infrastructure investment often requires choosing between an established technology and a capital-intensive alternative that gains value as demand matures. For electric vehicle (EV) charging, this trade-off is between incumbent stationary charging technology and emerging dynamic wireless charging (DWC). DWC could fundamentally alter transportation electrification by enabling high-throughput charging in motion and reducing reliance on large onboard batteries; however, its high upfront cost makes the timing and location of deployment critical. Overcommitting to stationary charging stations (SCS) risks technological lock-in and forgoing the benefits of DWC, whereas premature DWC deployment can strand capital in underutilized corridors. Through a joint investment assessment framework coupling DWC, SCS, and supporting grid infrastructure across nearly 49,000 miles of the US Interstate freight network, we find that higher utilization and longer project lifetimes rapidly shift investment toward DWC, whose share rises sharply from 48% at a project lifetime of 30 years to 100% at 32 years. Contiguous DWC segments can share grid connections, enabling them to provide over six times the rated charging capacity of SCS while requiring 46% less investment in new distribution-grid infrastructure. We also find that a combined DWC and SCS portfolio reaches a maximum lifetime value of USD 60 billion, 63% above the case with only SCS. We further identify specific traffic demand, construction, and grid access conditions that shape where each technology becomes advantageous, yielding actionable thresholds for SCS and DWC deployment that directly inform long-term EV charging infrastructure investment and policy.

Systems and Control.title: Uncertainty-Aware Parameter Estimation for Condition Monitoring of Power Converters
Systems and Control.summary: Changes in circuit parameters can indicate component degradation in power converters, but measurement noise and limited parameter observability can make these changes difficult to detect reliably. This paper proposes an uncertainty-aware parameter estimation framework to distinguish genuine parameter changes from variations caused by estimation uncertainty. Using a differentiable switched converter model, the method requires only one or two samples per switching period. Model-derived residual whitening and a Bayesian posterior approximation quantify estimation uncertainty and reveal poorly identifiable parameters. Simulations demonstrate improved estimation accuracy over least-squares and physics-informed neural-network benchmarks, with uncertainty estimates consistent with repeated noise realizations. Experiments on a laboratory buck converter validate the estimated parameters against independently derived references and demonstrate the detection of a controlled output-capacitance reduction. The proposed framework provides a basis for reliable parameter-change detection in power converter condition monitoring.

Logic in Computer Science.title: PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Even a carefully proofread paper can leave small gaps in its proofs or its stated assumptions. We introduce PaperFormalizer, a Lean-based agentic pipeline that helps authors find and close such gaps in their own papers and turn each paper into a Lean-verified version. Starting from the LaTeX source, PaperFormalizer transcribes the paper into a dependency graph of statements, audits each statement in natural language for faithfulness, ambiguity and correctness, and then formalizes and proves the statements in Lean against Mathlib, optional domain libraries and the author's personal toolkit. Only the author knows what a statement is meant to say and how a formalization gap in a result is best fixed. The pipeline therefore stops and asks the author whenever a statement admits more than one reading, presents every repair, in natural language and TeX symbols, as a proposal that the author can accept, decline or redirect, and leaves to the author every decision that could potentially change what the paper claims. The output is an annotated and revised version of the paper, a report of the changes, and Lean code in which each declaration is linked to the statement it formalizes. The author's toolkit grows as more papers are formalized, and authors can share their verified papers so that researchers who build on them can reuse their Lean code. By making verified papers practical to produce, PaperFormalizer aims to make research that rests on mathematical proofs more robust. PaperFormalizer runs inside a coding agent (Claude Code or Codex) and is available at https://github.com/Jiyuan-Tan/PaperFormalizer. Papers with Lean code shared by users are available at https://paperformalizer.org.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Reasoning about the Genetic Code in Lean
Logic in Computer Science.summary: The genetic code exhibits redundancy, meaning that multiple distinct nucleotide sequences can encode the same amino acid sequence, a property mathematically characterized as non-injectivity. While this phenomenon is well studied in molecular biology, its rigorous verification within a computational framework remains limited. In this work, we present a machine-verified model of the central dogma of molecular biology using the Lean 4 interactive theorem prover. We formalize nucleic acid bases and amino acids as inductive types and define transcription and translation as functions mapping DNA sequences to RNA and subsequently to polypeptides. Within this framework, we prove key properties of these biological processes, including the redundancy of the genetic code, injectivity of transcription, and the non-injectivity of translation. Additionally, we formalize auxiliary processes such as DNA replication and mutation, and verify properties such as length conservation under transcription and point mutations. Finally, we demonstrate how Lean 4 helps prevent semantic errors in our code, showing its effectiveness as a tool for advancing reliable, bug-free scientific computing, particularly within the life sciences.

Logic in Computer Science.title: How Stable Are LLM-Generated Proofs Under Program Refactoring? A Stress Test for Verifiable Code Generation
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Benchmarks for verifiable code generation usually test a proof against one fixed implementation. We ask whether the same proof remains valid after a program refactoring that preserves behavior. We introduce RefactorProof, which derives 458 Lean-certified variants from the 185 VERINA tasks that compile in our pinned environment while holding the specification and evaluated proof fixed byte-for-byte. VERINA supplies reference proofs for 46 tasks, all from its basic split; the primary model-versus-reference comparisons further match on 21-25 short, non-recursive tasks. Structural refactorings expose substantial brittleness across proof sources: task-normalized structural PSR is 4.3% for the supplied references and 13.3-26.8% for the specialized provers. On the matched tasks, specialized prover proofs nevertheless have higher overall unchanged-proof survival than the supplied reference artifacts: +15.6 points for DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B, +18.8 for Goedel-Prover-V2-32B, and +20.3 for Goedel-Prover-V2-8B; all three 95% CIs exclude zero. The ordering persists after excluding universally survived T1 variants, under family-balanced aggregation, and under alternative deployable valid-proof selection rules. However, unchanged-proof failure is not the same as high repair cost: predefined one-identifier edits repair 51/54 eligible reference structural failures and 58/85 eligible prover failures. RefactorProof therefore measures unchanged-proof stability under program refactoring, not the cost of maintaining a proof after it breaks.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on AI for Verifiable Coding

Logic in Computer Science.title: Demodalising Gödel's God? Ultrafilters, Rigidity and Modal Collapse Revisited
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Gödel's ontological argument is modal by design. Possibility and necessity are among its central concerns, and connected interpretation decisions -- extensions or intensions for the positive properties, constant or varying quantifier domains, the choice of modal logic, etc. -- subtly shape the argument and, in particular, whether the modal collapse is implied or not. It is tempting to abstract the modality away and to read the positive properties as merely forming an ultrafilter -- which, however, may replace Gödel's argument with a perhaps more manageable alternative that may have little to do with Gödel's original intention. In this spirit, Odifreddi and Gomes argue that modal collapse is an intrinsic structural feature of any theory that characterises positive properties as an ultrafilter and identifies God as its principal generator. This comment shows that the structural claim is false. There is an explicit S5 model, with constant domains, in which positivity is at every world a modal ultrafilter principally generated by a unique and necessarily existing Godlike individual, and in which the modal collapse nevertheless fails -- already for an atomic formula. What drives the collapse is not the ultrafilter structure but the rigidity of positivity -- itself a thoroughly modal condition: given only that positivity is a modal ultrafilter, modal collapse and rigidity are equivalent. Rigidity is thus exactly what the collapse adds to the ultrafilter structure, and the disagreement is whether it is to be counted part of that structure at all. Two further claims of Odifreddi and Gomes are clarified: one on the derivability of Gödel's Theorem IV, one on the extensionality of positivity. All results are machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL, which distinguishes kernel-checked proofs from model-finder output.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: 21 pages. Accepted for publication in Logica Universalis (revised version). Companion Isabelle/HOL session included as ancillary files (directory anc/GoedelUltrafilterNote); builds with Isabelle2025-2 in about 15 s. Previous title: "A Comment on Modal Collapse and Ultrafilters in Gödel's Ontological Argument"

Logic in Computer Science.title: Legislating World-Model-Based Planning with Legal Reasoning
Logic in Computer Science.summary: As robotic systems grow more general, legal norms are needed to integrate them into society. This paper extends the isomorphism problem of aligning legal source texts with their encodings, and measures two key challenges to robot normative control: (1) the grounding isomorphism gap, where perception error grounds false atoms for legal reasoning, and (2) the ontological isomorphism gap, where one legal conclusion admits many faithful translations into planning constraints. The paper introduces a legal planning stack that employs Defeasible Deontic Logic (DDL) to constrain a motion planner. The stack leverages learned world models to plan and to provide legal context, enabling ex ante governance that intervenes before an illegal action is executed. It was deployed on a simulated robot arm pushing a cube across a 3x3 grid. The findings were (1) the legislated agent abided substantially more often than the non-legislated one, and modeling perception uncertainty lifted abidance even further, (2) the legal reasoning ran efficiently at runtime and its verdicts were auditable, and (3) the stack adapted to exogenous signals and endogenous rule changes. Both gaps were measured: (4) world model and probe error corrupted the factual input for the DDL reasoner, and (5) a single law admitted several faithful metric interpretations yielding drastically different abidance. Thus, ex ante legislation functions as intended, and closing these gaps with a standardized mapping from the law to runtime constraints and improved fact grounding from perception will yield robust laws that align robot behavior with society's norms. Project page: https://dylanwaldner-cail.github.io/Legislated-Planner/.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: Project page: https://dylanwaldner-cail.github.io/Legislated-Planner/. Accepted at JURIX 2026

Logic in Computer Science.title: count-catcher: Lean Theorems from Model Counting Certificates
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We present count-catcher, a tool that turns a CPOG certificate of a count by the exact model counter d4 into a Lean theorem that a CNF formula defined in Lean has exactly N models over V variables. With an encoding lemma, this theorem becomes a theorem about the number of combinatorial objects. A CPOG certificate consists of a Boolean circuit equivalent to the formula and a proof of equivalence. count-catcher checks in Lean that the formula implies the circuit (forward check) and the circuit implies the formula (reverse check). For the forward check, lrat-catcher streams a refutation through the LRAT checker of Lean's standard library. The reverse check and the validity check of the circuit are computations proved correct in Lean. Lean runs all three checks as compiled code, so the theorem depends on Lean's kernel, compiler and runtime, as does CPOG's verified checker. We combine the theorem with results from Mathlib, for instance with Burnside's lemma to count graphs up to isomorphism. We prove the number of Latin squares of order 8 as a weighted sum of hundreds of certified counts from about eight terabytes of certificates. We turn about half of the 2022 Model Counting Competition formulas into theorems, with the three checks taking about a quarter of the time of CPOG's verified checker. We found that CPOG's unverified checker reported wrong counts, and removed its verified checker's dependence on two unproved lemmas. End to end, a theorem costs about the same as a checked count.

Logic in Computer Science.title: Replication or Corroboration? An Axiomatic Framework for Evidential Dependence in Multi-Agent Debate
Logic in Computer Science.summary: In multi-agent debates, matching reports can arise for two different reasons: agents may repeat the same evidence (replication), or they may provide separate evidential roots that support the same claim (corroboration). A judge must distinguish these two cases. Counting report occurrences gives extra weight to relays, paraphrases, alias resubmissions, and excerpt splits, while merging all matching content avoids this only by also removing genuine corroboration. We formalize this tension as a minimal judgment game in which acquiring new evidence is costly, but replication is cheap. We show that root replication invariance (RRI) is exactly threshold-uniform replication immunity. Under RRI, replication-only deviations cannot change the verdict, and positive-cost replication is strictly dominated, whereas occurrence-sensitive and content-keyed judges admit profitable deviations. We also establish an information boundary: if a judge's observation interface cannot distinguish a replica from a matched fresh root, no judge can both ignore the replica and respond strictly to the fresh root. To preserve this distinction, we introduce the lineage quotient, which removes wording, identity, occurrence multiplicity, and arbitrary root names while keeping distinct roots separate. On orbit-connected domains, it is the coarsest representation sufficient for every deterministic judge invariant to replication and root-label renaming. We further lift this construction to quantitative bipolar argumentation frameworks (QBAFs), characterize strict fresh-root response, prove its propagation along sign-consistent paths under DF-QuAD, and derive a tight closed-form response modulus. Exhaustive audits over 28,224 direct-star profiles, 2,052 multi-layer DAGs, with matched interventions on 277 AVeriTeC-derived profiles, show the predicted separation between replication and corroboration under a supplied partition.

Logic in Computer Science.title: The Undecidability of FO3 and the Calculus of Relations with Just One Binary Relation
Logic in Computer Science.summary: The validity problem for first-order logic is a well-known undecidable problem. The undecidability also holds even for $\mathsf{FO}3$ and (equational formulas of) the calculus of relations. In this paper we tighten these undecidability results to the following: (1) $\mathsf{FO}3$ with just one binary relation is undecidable even without equality; and (2) the calculus of relations with just one character and with only composition, union, and complement is undecidable. Additionally we prove that the finite validity problem is also undecidable for the above two classes.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: Long version of the paper at ICLA'19, with (Ax.1) and (Ax.2) in Section 3 corrected

Logic in Computer Science.title: A meta-modal logic for bisimulations
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We propose a novel modal study of bisimulations. Our contribution is threefold. First, we extend the basic modal language with a new modality $\nbi$, whose intended meaning is universal quantification over all states that are bisimilar to the current one under a given bisimulation. We show that bisimulations are definable in this object language via frame validity (for the forth and back conditions) and model validity (for the atomic harmony condition). Additionally, some other related notions (refinements, simulations, bisimulations for a restricted set of variables, and $n$-bisimulations) are also shown to be definable. Second, we provide a sound and complete axiomatisation of the class of all pairs of Kripke models that are bisimulation-related. Third, we show that the satisfiability problem of this logic is decidable and PSPACE-complete via a translation to standard modal logic $K$ under a simple frame condition. All our results are encoded and verified by Isabelle/HOL.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: 22 pages

Logic in Computer Science.title: The Proof-Theoretic Foundations of the Principle of Reiteration in Natural Deduction
Logic in Computer Science.summary: This paper investigates the proof-theoretic foundations of the principle of reiteration (R) in natural deduction, arguing that its legitimacy originates in the structural preservation of formulae within sequent calculus rather than in an independent logical rule. By examining singlesuccedent and multisuccedent sequent calculus, we demonstrate how logical operations transform principal formulae while preserving unaffected antecedent and succedent contexts. We subsequently analyse the schematic formulation of reiteration and compare natural deduction derivations with corresponding sequent calculus derivations. This comparison identifies two fundamental functions of reiteration, namely the reuse of previously employed formulae and the restoration of previously derived conclusions. We conclude that reiteration introduces no independent inferential content but explicitly represents the structural continuity of inferential dependencies already included into sequent calculus.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: 14 Pages

Logic in Computer Science.title: The Qualitative Collapse of Concurrent Games (Extended Version)
Logic in Computer Science.summary:
In this paper, we construct an interpretation-preserving functor from a category of concurrent games to the category of Scott domains and Scott-continuous functions. We give a concrete description of this functor, extending earlier results on the relational collapse of game semantics. The crux is an intricate combinatorial lemma allowing us to synchronize states of strategies which reach the same resources, but with different multiplicity.

Putting this together with the previously established relational collapse, this provides a new proof of the qualitative-quantitative correspondence first established by Ehrhard in his celebrated extensional collapse theorem. Whereas Ehrhard's proof is indirect and rests on an abstract realizability construction, our result gives a concrete, combinatorial description of the extraction of quantitative information from a qualitative model.

Logic in Computer Science.title: KAPPA: Checking the Proofs in Statistics Papers with Lean 4 and Language Model Agents
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Papers in statistical theory rest on long proofs that few readers check line by line. We present KAPPA (Kit of Agents for Proof-checking Papers with a proof Assistant), open-source software that organizes language model agents, run by Claude Code, to translate the proofs of a LaTeX paper into the proof assistant Lean 4 with its library Mathlib and check them there, result by result. Each numbered result receives one of four verdicts: verified unconditionally; verified conditionally, with every cited or unproved input stated as a named hypothesis; issue recorded, with its place in the paper and the side at fault; or unfinished, with the reason. The kit follows the paper's own proof step by step, rather than finding a new one. Separate agents write and review, each statement is compared with the paper before it is proved and fingerprinted afterwards, and every verdict rests on evidence that can be rerun without a language model. The kit runs unattended for hours, waits out usage limits, re-checks only what a revision changed and reports its cost by role, model and result. We describe the design, walk through a complete run, and apply the kit to four example papers with answer keys and to three published statistical papers, checked blind in their versions from before public corrections. In all three, the kit found the published error at the step that the correction names, together with further problems that we confirmed by hand. Given the same papers directly, the same language model working with Lean classified fewer results correctly on the longest paper and reported some statements narrower than the paper's as proved; no verdict of the kit claimed more than its Lean evidence showed.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: 31 pages, 2 figures. Software: https://github.com/ziwaa-se/kappa

Logic in Computer Science.title: Goedel Logics: On the Elimination of The Absoluteness Operator
Logic in Computer Science.summary: We investigate the eliminability of the absoluteness operator Delta in Goedel logics. While Delta is not definable from the standard connectives and disrupts important proof-theoretic properties, we show that it becomes eliminable at the propositional level under a non-standard semantics in which all propositional atoms (except the truth constant 'True') are interpreted strictly below 1. Under this semantics, every formula containing Delta is equivalent to a disjunction of chain formulas, yielding a Delta-free normal form (standard and non-standard semantics coincide w.r.t. valid formulas without Delta). We further analyze the situation in the first-order setting, where Delta-elimination fails in general due to recursion-theoretic and topological constraints, but can be recovered under witnessed semantics.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: This research was funded in part by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) 10.55776/P36571. To be appeared in TbiLLC 2025 Postproceedings

Logic in Computer Science.title: Interaction Improvement
Logic in Computer Science.summary: The relational semantics of linear logic is a powerful framework for defining resource-aware models of the $λ$-calculus. However, its quantitative aspects are not reflected in the preorders and equational theories induced by these models. Indeed, they can be characterized in terms of (in)equalities between Böhm trees up to extensionality, which are qualitative in nature. We employ the recently introduced checkers calculus to define a quantitative contextual preorder on $λ$-terms, and demonstrate that it coincides with the preorder associated to the relational semantics.
Logic in Computer Science.comment: Version with proofs of the FoSSaCS 2026 paper

Logic in Computer Science.title: Ranking Function Generation with LLMs for Termination
Logic in Computer Science.summary: Ranking functions are a fundamental technique for proving loop termination, but constructing them manually is challenging and requires substantial expertise. We propose RAINFALL, a neuro-symbolic framework which follows the generate-verify-refine paradigm and tightly integrates LLMs with symbolic verification. RAINFALL formulates ranking function synthesis as a code-completion task by inserting placeholders into the input program and constraining the LLM to fill four predefined slots for each loop. The completed program is then checked by a symbolic verifier. If verification succeeds, a valid ranking function is obtained; otherwise, the verifier's diagnostics are translated into natural-language feedback that guides iterative refinement of the LLM's output. We evaluate RAINFALL on two public benchmark suites comprising 358 terminating C programs. Using MiniMax V2.7, RAINFALL synthesizes verifiable ranking functions for 323 programs (90.22%), outperforming all promising baselines. In particular, it solves 12 more programs than PROTON 2.1, the best-performing baseline and winner of the SV-COMP 2026 Termination category. Furthermore, combining RAINFALL with PROTON 2.1 increases the success rate to 96.65% (346/358 programs). We also conduct ablation study confirming individual contributions of placeholder contracts, few-shot examples, symbolic verification, and diagnostic information feedback. Experiments across LLMs further confirm the effectiveness of RAINFALL.
